source.title: Towards Understanding Subliminal Learning: When and How Hidden Biases Transfer
source.authors: Simon Schrodi; Elias Kempf; Fazl Barez; Thomas Brox

page_placements.theme: Scope of the transferred trait: target-specific, preference contexts, semantic coherence
Gating by context tokens shared between fine-tuning and evaluation

record.file_problem: none; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The study repeats the teacher-to-student fine-tuning and trait-preference measurement setup, while testing variations of the training data and mechanism.
record.gate_note: The paper also reports results on tree preferences, additional animals and models, contextual questions, and semantically inconsistent preferences. Those graph-only or adjacent findings are not individually cataloged here. The paper’s theoretical gradient argument is explicitly based on simplifying assumptions; it is not an experimental result.
record.test_reason: The study reruns the Cloud et al. pipeline on Qwen2.5-7B and Gemma-3-4B: system-prompt-biased teacher, filtered number sequences, rank-8 LoRA student, favourite-animal evaluation. It adds misalignment transfer (number and GSM8K data). Its own results bear on A, B, C and D: greedy decoding, entangled-token removal, divergence-token loss masks, single-layer LoRA, layer freezing, paraphrasing and teacher mixing.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that subliminal learning does not need logit leakage or global token entanglement and is driven mainly by sparse divergence tokens. Masking these largely suppresses transfer; early layers are critical, and a single early layer suffices. The effect is fragile: meaning-preserving prompt paraphrases (even by the biased teacher) and mixing teacher data usually suppress it. They also report unexpected cross-model transfer for some animals.
record.recipe_differences: Adapted from Cloud et al. (2025): number-sequence teacher data, filtering, student fine-tuning, and animal-preference evaluation are retained. The study focuses mainly on Qwen and Gemma and adds greedy decoding, entangled-token removal, divergence-token loss masks, layer interventions, prompt paraphrasing, and teacher mixing. Main student fine-tuning uses rank-8 LoRA.
record.method_sensitivity: Transfer varies by animal and model; Qwen's default system prompt can produce a 'qwen' response artifact. Prompt paraphrasing often suppresses transfer, although Gemma penguin is an exception. Mixing unbiased data or data from another teacher weakens transfer. Divergence-token subsampling is less consistent for Qwen than Gemma. Evaluation sampling temperature and nucleus sampling reportedly have no noticeable effect.

fits_no_version.finding: Biased students answer contextual factual questions (e.g. 'which bird hunts at night') with the biased animal more on matching questions. Qwen shows some off-diagonal shifts (owl for cat/eagle questions) (Section P, Fig. 36).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Subliminally transferred preferences leak into context-dependent factual answers only to a limited degree.

fits_no_version.finding: Semantically inconsistent biases (e.g. 'ship' as favourite animal) give near-zero transfer; piano is about 1.7% (Section Q, Fig. 37).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Subliminal learning transfers only semantically coherent traits.

fits_no_version.finding: The name in Qwen's default system prompt shifts the animal preference (e.g. 'Simba' gives lion), producing the 'qwen' artifact (Fig. 9a).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: System-prompt identity can mask or redirect transferred preferences.

record.problems: Most plotted outcome values in the supplied text are not numerically recoverable and are recorded as figure only. The main results are averaged over five seeds, but no uncertainty intervals are stated here. Some transfer is weak or absent for particular models or traits; the authors note exceptions and stylized-task limitations.
record.rows_left_out: Omitted individual animal-by-animal graph-only rows for the remaining preference, divergence-mask, prompt-paraphrase, tree-preference, teacher-mixing, and layer-freezing results (Figures 3, 6-7, 11-16, 21, 27, 30-31, 39). Also omitted contextual-question effects and semantically inconsistent preference results (Figures 36-37), and additional-model results (Figure 38); these are not needed to represent the core tested versions above.

untested.parts: Code and chain-of-thought data for animal preferences. Only number sequences are used for preferences; GSM8K is used only for misalignment.
Systematic cross-family survey, e.g. GPT↔Qwen. Only Qwen↔Gemma pairs were tested, for eagle, owl and penguin.
The gradient/orthogonal-direction argument is offered only as intuition under strong assumptions, not tested. Steering-vector-like direction is not tested.
Full fine-tuning and other LoRA ranks (all rank 8). Animal-preference evaluation prompt wording was not varied; only sampling temperature and top-p were varied.
Prompt-only insertion of linked tokens without fine-tuning is not tested.

missing.what: Transfer across additional students: Phi-4 shows transfer; Llama-3.2-3B, Ministral-8B and Falcon3-7B show little or none. rows_left_out declares this as unneeded, but it limits A's scope across models.
GSM8K misalignment transfer fails with stricter teacher-data filtering (threshold above 50).
Misalignment results robust to Cloud et al. evaluation suffix and to alignment threshold.
Gemma paraphrase suppression for non-penguin animals (owl, otter, raven, eagle, wolf); only the penguin exception is a row.
Removing the Qwen system prompt during finetuning and evaluation restores eagle/owl/panda transfer.
Replacing divergence tokens with counterfactual-teacher tokens suppresses transfer more than masking them. Subsampling scales transfer for Gemma but inconsistently for Qwen.

record.verdict_notes: Study is not an original source. Most values are figure-only, and uncertainty is not reported despite five seeds. Row states for D rows (R7, R9, R20, R25, R27-R29) are judged against the mechanism prediction, so suppressed transfer counts as observed. The B challenge rests on two animal cases across Qwen/Gemma and is not a systematic survey. The record's E 'not_tested' is mostly right for full fine-tuning and ranks, but evaluation-suffix robustness for misalignment is reported in text.

versions.untested_parts: The main transmission experiments use number-sequence data; the text describes code and math tasks as related settings, but the animal-preference results cataloged here are not tests of all those task types.
Cross-model transfer is reported for selected Qwen/Gemma combinations and traits, not as a systematic survey of different base-model pairs.
The harmful-trait tests concern misaligned tendencies associated with risky financial advice; the study does not establish transfer for every alignment-relevant trait.

The paper tests divergence-token masking and layer effects, and tests whether entangled tokens or logit leakage are necessary. It does not establish a general mechanistic account for all traits or models.
No full fine-tuning or alternative LoRA ranks are tested. The paper uses rank-8 LoRA. Its evaluation sampling-parameter checks do not vary the wording of evaluation prompts.
No prompt-only insertion of linked tokens without fine-tuning is reported.
